title: Insufficient color contrast
user_impact: Text is hard to read for people with low vision or under poor lighting conditions.
technical_impact: Contrast ratio below 4.5:1 for normal text.

checks.source: WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.3 Contrast (Minimum); definitions 'contrast ratio', 'relative luminance', 'large scale (text)'
checks.applicability: Every element that itself carries rendered, visible text (own non-empty text node; not display:none, visibility:hidden or visually hidden), in the top document, open shadow roots and frames.
checks.expectation:
Fails when the contrast ratio between the text colour actually painted
(-webkit-text-fill-color wins over color; a translucent foreground is
composited) and the effective background is below 4.5:1, or below 3:1 for
large text (at least 18pt = 24px, or 14pt = 18.66px bold). WCAG forbids
rounding up: 4.48:1 fails, 2.96:1 fails for large text; 4.54:1 and 3.03:1
pass. Text that is not rendered or only visually hidden is not visible text
and is not measured. Text under aria-hidden is still visible text and is
measured (1.4.3 is about what is seen, not the accessibility tree). Text in
a shadow root or a frame is part of the page. A viewport-specific colour
counts in the viewport where it applies; a colour set by script after load
counts as rendered. When the background cannot be resolved (gradient,
background-clip:text, covered by an overlay) the rule does not guess: that
is contrast/text-undetermined, never a pass or fail here.

When the page declares a dark colour scheme (@media (prefers-color-scheme:
dark), a color-scheme naming dark) it is measured a second time with
prefers-color-scheme: dark emulated, and what fails there is reported under
this same id with the computed evidence attribute color_scheme: dark (#917).
Text that passes on the default render but fails under the dark scheme (and
the reverse) is judged per scheme; a failure that is identical in both
schemes (same element, same colours) is one finding, not two. Only confirmed
failures of the top document are carried over from the dark render.

failing.html:
Low contrast body text

This paragraph uses light gray text on a white background, well below the 4.5:1 contrast ratio required for normal-size body text.

passing.html:
Text fill color overrides color

This paragraph declares dark text but paints its glyphs light gray through -webkit-text-fill-color, below the required 4.5:1 ratio.

This paragraph declares light gray text but paints its glyphs almost black through -webkit-text-fill-color, which passes comfortably.
